entries.definition: to watch carefully to learn about something
entries.example: We observe the birds without moving closer to their nest.

entries.definition: to find the size or amount of something
entries.example: Use this ruler to measure the length of the leaf.

entries.definition: how hot or cold something is
entries.example: Check the water temperature before adding the seeds.

entries.definition: force acting on a surface
entries.example: The pump increases the pressure inside the tire.

entries.definition: how heavy something is
entries.example: The bridge has a sign showing its weight limit.

entries.definition: the distance from one end of something to the other
entries.example: Write the length of each piece on the box.

entries.definition: the space between two places or things
entries.example: We estimated the distance between the two trees.

entries.definition: how fast something moves or happens
entries.example: The driver reduced speed near the school.

entries.definition: the outside or top layer of something
entries.example: Place the jar on a flat surface.

entries.definition: a substance used to make something
entries.example: We chose a light material for the model bridge.

entries.definition: a substance that flows and takes a container’s shape
entries.example: Pour the liquid slowly into the smaller bottle.

entries.definition: a substance with a firm shape rather than flowing freely
entries.example: Ice is a solid that can turn into water.

entries.definition: a substance that spreads to fill available space
entries.example: The diagram shows how gas moves through the pipe.

entries.definition: the capacity to cause movement or other changes
entries.example: The solar panel provides energy for a small lamp.

entries.definition: energy that moves from a hotter object to a cooler one
entries.example: The handle protects your hand from the heat.

entries.definition: the energy that makes things visible
entries.example: The curtain blocks most of the morning light.

entries.definition: vibrations that can be heard
entries.example: The soft sound came from a loose window.

entries.definition: a push or pull acting on something
entries.example: A gentle force was enough to move the empty box.

entries.definition: the act or process of moving
entries.example: The drawing shows the wheel’s motion with arrows.

entries.definition: the attraction between objects that have mass
entries.example: Gravity pulls the dropped ball toward the ground.

entries.definition: an object that attracts certain metals
entries.example: The small magnet picked up the steel pin.

entries.definition: a material such as iron or copper
entries.example: The metal handle became warm in the sun.

entries.definition: a manufactured material that can be shaped
entries.example: We reused the plastic container to store buttons.

entries.definition: a hard transparent material used for windows and containers
entries.example: The glass lid lets us see inside the pot.

entries.definition: a substance with a particular composition
entries.example: Read the label before using any cleaning chemical.

entries.definition: two or more substances put together
entries.example: The mixture contains water, flour, and a little salt.

entries.definition: to mix into a liquid until separate pieces disappear
entries.example: Stir the sugar until it begins to dissolve.

entries.definition: to become solid because of low temperature
entries.example: Water may freeze in the outdoor pipe tonight.

entries.definition: to change from a solid into a liquid through warming
entries.example: The ice will melt faster on the warm plate.

entries.definition: to heat a liquid until it bubbles strongly
entries.example: We boil the water before making our tea.

entries.definition: a gas in air needed for human breathing
entries.example: The lesson explains how oxygen enters the blood.

entries.definition: a chemical element found in living things and many materials
entries.example: The class found carbon in several different diagrams.

entries.definition: a basic living unit of an organism
entries.example: The picture shows the parts of a plant cell.

entries.definition: a body part with a particular function
entries.example: The heart is an organ that pumps blood.

entries.definition: a particular kind of plant, animal, or other living thing
entries.example: The guide described one species of mountain bird.

entries.definition: a place equipped for scientific tests
entries.example: Students wear protective glasses inside the laboratory.

entries.definition: an instrument that makes very small things look larger
entries.example: We used a microscope to examine an onion cell.

entries.definition: an instrument that makes distant objects look closer
entries.example: The telescope helped us see more detail on the Moon.

entries.definition: a small part taken to examine a larger whole
entries.example: Each team collected a soil sample from a different place.

entries.definition: what happens or is found after an action or test
entries.example: The result surprised us, so we checked our notes.

entries.definition: a repeated form or regular way something happens
entries.example: A pattern appeared when we arranged the measurements.

entries.definition: something that makes an event or change happen
entries.example: The team searched for the cause of the leak.

entries.definition: a change produced by an action or condition
entries.example: Shade had a noticeable effect on the soil temperature.

entries.definition: the act of finding something previously unknown
entries.example: The unexpected discovery led to a new question.

entries.definition: to say what you think will happen
entries.example: Can you predict which paper bridge will hold more weight?

entries.definition: to examine something to find out how it works
entries.example: We will test both filters with the same water.

entries.definition: a comparison condition used in an experiment
entries.example: The untreated plant served as the control in our experiment.

entries.definition: a factor that can change in a test or situation
entries.example: The amount of water was the only variable we changed.

entries.definition: recorded facts or measurements used for analysis
entries.example: Our data includes the height of each plant.

entries.definition: a series of events that repeats in order
entries.example: The diagram follows the cycle from seed to new seeds.
